title: Introduce probabilistic eviction gate and probationary rejoin guard
author: Aisha Martinez
release_notes: Adds probabilistic eviction gate and probationary rejoin guard to reduce mass-eviction cascades during transient spikes. New runtime knobs behind feature flag, additional metrics and dashboards, and a safe canary rollout plan.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated mass-eviction events during short-lived regional spikes where deterministic eviction + synchronous rejoin caused cascading SLO degradation (incident notes: Linear ENG-4821). This PR introduces a probabilistic eviction gate to avoid synchronized mass eviction and a probationary rejoin guard that stages tenant re-enablement with progressive warmup, reducing sudden pressure on downstream nodes. The implementation is deliberately conservative and behind a feature flag for canarying.

What changed (summary):
- New probabilistic eviction gate that computes a per-tenant eviction probability using tenant penalty score, global pressure factor, and a configurable randomness seed. The algorithm biases against evicting many tenants at once during transients.
- Probationary rejoin guard: tenants that were evicted enter a staged rejoin window where they are admitted at a controlled rate (token-bucket warmup + success-based backoff).
- Integration with existing SLO enforcement and circuit-breaker: eviction decisions now consult circuit state and regional health probes before applying eviction.
- Observability: new metrics (eviction_probability, probationary_rejoin_attempts, probationary_rejoin_success_rate, staged_rejoin_tokens), plus dashboards and traces for debugging rejoin ramps.
- Configuration: runtime.shedding.probabilistic_eviction.{enabled,base_rate,burst_suppression,seed} and runtime.shedding.rejoin.{stages,token_rate,success_window}. Defaults are conservative and documented.
- Tests: unit tests for distribution behavior, integration test simulating short regional spike, and a small canary e2e harness.
- Docs: added operational runbook describing when to enable, how to tune knobs, and related alerts.

Design notes:
- Probabilistic eviction reduces correlated eviction by sampling tenants with a computed probability instead of a hard cutoff. The gate still respects per-tenant SLO priorities and absolute safety limits (we never evict critical-tier tenants unless explicit override).
- The rejoin guard is stateful for the probationary window (short-lived in-memory token buckets), with best-effort persistence across restarts via small checkpoints. The design avoids long-lived state to keep operational complexity low.
- We intentionally keep the defaults conservative (probability floor, low token rate) when the feature flag is on; operators should validate on non-critical regions first.

Testing and canary plan:
- Unit suite: coverage added for core math and edge cases (0 probability, 100% suppression).
- Integration: simulated regional spike test that asserts no more than X% simultaneous evictions vs previous deterministic algorithm.
- Canary rollout: enable in staging region for 24h, then enable in one low-traffic production region for 6h with traffic shadowing and telemetry checks. If probationary_rejoin_success_rate < 95% or staged_rejoin_tokens exhausted frequently, rollback.

CI: initial run returned a flaky integration failure (timing-dependent test). Reworked the test (commit e5f7g9h) to use deterministic seeding; rerun passed. CI matrix: unit, linters, integration(canary), e2e-shadow. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (abridged):
- Marcus Li (reviewer): "Nice approach — probabilistic gate should reduce synchronized evictions. Please add a unit test for the 0->1 boundary when global_pressure oscillates quickly and ensure sample seed is deterministic for tests."
- Aisha (author): "Added deterministic seeding and an edge-case unit test. Also added a short note in the runbook about tuning seed and windows for canarying."
- Eloise Tan (reviewer): "Can we add a metric that reports 'eviction_batched' when the gate intentionally suppresses a batch? That will help on-call correlate incidents."
- Aisha: "Added eviction_suppressed_count metric and dashboard panel."
- Ravi Patel (approver): "Looks good. Verified integration test results on staging. Approving."

Operational considerations / Alerts changed:
- New alert SLO: ProbationaryRejoinDegraded if probationary_rejoin_success_rate < 90% for 10m in canary regions.
- Adjusted existing eviction rate alert to include eviction_probability composition to avoid noisy paging during controlled rollouts.

Merge and rollout: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-20. Feature flag default: off in production. Canary enabled via examples/canary/probabilistic-eviction.yaml.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-4829: Add multi-region coordination mode to bias rejoin tokens away from simultaneously rejoining tenants in different regions.
- Short-term: add a tiny HSM-backed seed option for improved entropy across restarts.
- Observability: build an aggregated heatmap of staged_rejoin_tokens usage per-tenant cohort (next sprint).

Notes for on-call: if you see a spike in eviction_suppressed_count with rising queue_length and sustained latency, consider temporarily lowering base_rate and increasing token_rate for the probationary rejoin guard. Runbook section points to docs/operational-eviction.md for exact commands and config keys.
